1.note: These two clauses mean basically the same thing. The second emphasizes the meaning of the first by repeating the same idea with different words. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could combine them and express the emphasis in another way. Alternate translation: [Always do what is just and right]

If your language does not use abstract nouns for the ideas of **justice** and **righteousness**, you could express the same ideas in other ways. Alternate translation: [Keep what is just and do what is right]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **salvation**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [the time when I will save you]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **righteousness**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [and my righteous deeds]

The expression **to being revealed** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [which I am about to reveal]

Isaiah is leaving out some of the words that in many languages a sentence would need in order to be complete. You can supply these words from the context if that would be clearer in your language. Alternate translation: [and my righteousness is near to being revealed]

2.note: Isaiah is using a phrase that expresses a strong feeling of happiness or blessedness. There may be an equivalent word or phrase in your language that you can use in your translation to convey this feeling. Alternate translation: [How blessed is the man]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **happiness**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [How happy is]

Here the masculine term **the man** has a generic sense that includes both men and women. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could use language in your translation that is clearly inclusive of both men and women. Alternate translation: [the person]

Isaiah is using **the son of man** as a common expression of the culture to mean “a human being.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [and the person]

Here, **his hand** represents “his actions.” If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [and keeping himself from doing any evil]

3.note: Isaiah is using **son of** as a common expression of the culture to indicate that a person has a certain characteristic. In this case, the person has the characteristic of being a foreigner, that is, someone who is not an Israelite. If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning or state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [the foreigner]

Isaiah is repeating forms of the verb **say** in order to intensify his expression of the idea that it conveys. If your language can repeat words for intensification, it would be appropriate to do that here in your translation. If not, your language may have another way of expressing the intensification. Alternate translation: [lament]

This is a quotation within a quotation. If it would be clearer in your language, you could translate this so that there is not a quotation within a quotation. Alternate translation: [that Yahweh will surely separate him from his people]

Isaiah is repeating forms of the verb **separate** in order to intensify his expression of the idea that it conveys. If your language can repeat words for intensification, it would be appropriate to do that here in your translation. If not, your language may have another way of expressing the intensification. Alternate translation: [Yahweh will certainly separate me]
The pronoun **his** refers to Yahweh. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [God’s people]

Isaiah is using the term **Behold** to focus his listeners’ attention on what he is about to say. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation. Alternate translation: [Listen]

The eunuch is speaking of himself as if he were **a dry tree** that cannot produce fruit, because he cannot father children. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [Behold, I am unable to have children]

This is a quotation within a quotation. If it would be clearer in your language, you could translate this so that there is not a quotation within a quotation. Alternate translation: [that he is only a dry tree]

5.note: Yahweh shifts from the plural pronoun **them**, which refers to the eunuchs as a group, to the singular pronoun **him**, which refers to each individual eunuch. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [I will give to all of them … I will give to each one of them]

The phrase **a hand and a name** expresses a single idea. In this context, the word **hand** means a “monument” or “memorial” (as in 2 Samuel 18:18), and the word **name** tells what kind of memorial this will be. It will be one that preserves and proclaims the reputation of a eunuch such as Yahweh is describing. If it would be more natural in your language, you could express this meaning in a different way. Alternate translation: [a celebratory monument]

It seems that Yahweh is speaking of these eunuchs each having a **hand** or monument in the temple area to represent how their reputation or **name** will last in the memory of the worshiping community. Alternate translation: [a lasting reputation]

The expression **that will not be cut off** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [that no one will ever destroy]

Yahweh is speaking of ending or destroying someone’s reputation as if it were something that could be **cut off**. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [that will never end]

6.note: Isaiah is using **sons of** as a common expression of the culture to indicate that a person has a certain characteristic. In this case, these people have the characteristic of being foreign. If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning or state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [foreigners]

6.q: עַל־יְהוָה֙ לְ⁠שָׁ֣רְת֔⁠וֹ וּֽ⁠לְ⁠אַהֲבָה֙ אֶת־שֵׁ֣ם יְהוָ֔ה לִ⁠הְי֥וֹת ל֖⁠וֹ לַ⁠עֲבָדִ֑ים
6.note: Here, **to** marks **to serve him** as the goal or purpose for which the foreigners are **joining themselves to Yahweh**. Use a connector in your language that makes it clear that this is the purpose. Alternate translation: [so that they can serve Yahweh and love the name of Yahweh and be his servants]

Here, **the name of Yahweh** represents “Yahweh himself.” If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [and to love Yahweh himself]

7.note: If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **holiness**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [my holy mountain]

By **the mountain of my holiness**, Yahweh means Mount Zion, where his temple stood. You could indicate this explicitly in your translation if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [Mount Zion, my holy mountain]
Here, **house** represents “the temple.” If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [in my temple of prayer]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **prayer**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [people praying to me]

Yahweh is using the possessive form **house of my prayer** to mean a house where people pray to him. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [in the house where people pray to me]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **acceptance**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [will be acceptable]

The expression **will be called** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [people will call my house a house of prayer]

8.note: The pronouns **him** and **his** refer to Israel, spoken of as a single group. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [yet I will gather more people to Israel, to its already gathered ones]

8.q: מְקַבֵּ֖ץ נִדְחֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל ע֛וֹד אֲקַבֵּ֥ץ עָלָ֖י⁠ו לְ⁠נִקְבָּצָֽי⁠ו
8.note: Yahweh is repeating forms of the verb **gather** in order to intensify his expression of the idea that it conveys. If your language can repeat words for intensification, it would be appropriate to do that here in your translation. If not, your language may have another way of expressing the intensification. Alternate translation: [the one gathering the outcasts of Israel—yet I will surely gather even more people to him, in addition to those I have already gathered]

The expression **gathered ones** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [to those whom I have gathered]

9.note: Isaiah is using the words **Every beast of the field, come to devour** to introduce a new part of his message. Use a word, phrase, or other method in your language that is natural for introducing a new event.

9.q: כֹּ֖ל חַיְת֣וֹ שָׂדָ֑י אֵתָ֕יוּ לֶ⁠אֱכֹ֥ל כָּל־חַיְת֖וֹ בַּ⁠יָּֽעַר
9.note: Yahweh is speaking of the nations that will attack Israel as if they were wild animals coming to **devour** their prey. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [Come and attack Israel, all you enemy nations]

10.note: Isaiah is speaking of Israel’s leaders as if they were **watchmen** who are **blind**, because they fail to see and warn the people about danger. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [His guardians fail to perceive and warn of danger]
The pronoun **His** refers to the people of Israel, whose leaders these watchmen represent. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [Israel’s watchmen]

10.q: כֻּלָּ⁠ם֙ כְּלָבִ֣ים אִלְּמִ֔ים לֹ֥א יוּכְל֖וּ לִ⁠נְבֹּ֑חַ
10.note: Isaiah is speaking of Israel’s leaders as if they were **mute dogs**, which are **not able to bark**, because they fail to warn the people of danger. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [All of them fail to warn the people of danger]

10.q: כֻּלָּ⁠ם֙ כְּלָבִ֣ים אִלְּמִ֔ים לֹ֥א יוּכְל֖וּ לִ⁠נְבֹּ֑חַ
10.note: These two clauses mean basically the same thing. The second emphasizes the meaning of the first by repeating the same idea with different words. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could combine them and express the emphasis in another way. Alternate translation: [They are all like dogs that cannot even bark]

Isaiah is speaking of the leaders’ failure to do their duty as if they were **dreaming, lying down**, and **loving to sleep**. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [distracted, idle, ones who love their own comfort]

11.note: Isaiah is speaking of Israel’s leaders as if they were **dogs** with such a strong appetite that **they do not know satiety**, that is, they are never satisfied. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [And these leaders are greedy; they are never satisfied]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **satiety**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [when they are satisfied]

Isaiah is speaking of Israel’s leaders as if they were **shepherds** who **do not know to discern**, that is, who fail to guide and protect the people as a shepherd cares for sheep. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [And they are leaders who do not know how to guide the people]

Isaiah is speaking of the conduct of the leaders as if it were a road, saying that they have all **turned to their way**. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [All of them do as they please]

Isaiah says **All of them** as an extreme statement for emphasis. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use a different way to express the emphasis. Alternate translation: [Nearly every one of them]

Isaiah is leaving out some of the words that in many languages a sentence would need in order to be complete. You can supply these words from the context if that would be clearer in your language. Alternate translation: [each man has turned to his own gain, every one of them]

Here the masculine term **a man** has a generic sense that includes both men and women. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could use language in your translation that is clearly inclusive of both men and women. Alternate translation: [each person to their own gain]

12.note: This is a quotation within a quotation. If it would be clearer in your language, you could translate this so that there is not a quotation within a quotation. Alternate translation: [They say that they should get wine and drink a lot of beer]

The leaders are leaving out some of the words that in many languages a sentence would need in order to be complete. You can supply these words from the context if that would be clearer in your language. Alternate translation: [it will be even greater, with much abundance]
